main_issue: How Agent D can keep cooking strong-smelling fish curry without the smell disrupting A's work calls, B's room and C's laundry

A-B.evidence: A asked for no strong-smelling cooking (T1); B said time doesn't help (T8) and later accepted the window and hood (T23). A never addressed B's proposal and did not comment on the final arrangement.

A-C.evidence: A wanted cooking after 7pm or Saturday (T5). C's final Tue/Thu/weekend (T21) overlaps with A's request (after 7pm, Saturday), but they never addressed each other directly.

A-D.evidence: D agreed to A's after-7pm or Saturday request (T6); A thanked D (T7); the final plan (T18, T22, T27) keeps within A's request.

B-C.evidence: B suggested the window and hood (T14); C said it wouldn't be enough for the laundry (T15). Later both accepted D's plan (T21, T23).

B-D.evidence: B said the timing doesn't help (T8, T20); D offered to open the window and use the hood every time (T22); B said 'Yes, please' (T23); D said 'settled' (T27).

C-D.evidence: C first asked for weekends only (T11); D questioned this (T12, T16); C then narrowed it to Mon/Wed/Fri evenings only (T17); D proposed Tue/Thu/weekend (T18); C agreed (T21).
